answer: Payment sits in escrow until a panel grades the delivered task, and every failed submission lands on a public board with the account name attached. A fresh nonce per submission blocks replay, so one decent answer cannot be copied by a raven's nest of clones, since the second copy dies before grading. What the design cannot do is stop a patient operator from slowly earning escrow on real work. It only makes fakery cost more than it returns, and the board is the atlas of attempts that later requesters read before hiring, the cedar post the whole scheme leans on.
